t.6.88.1: When that missile was repelled, Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, grew twice as wrathful, and in his wrath he at once made ready another missile.
t.6.88.2: Then the greatly radiant Rāvaṇa began to discharge at Rāghava another weapon, fierce and terrible, which had been fashioned by Maya.
t.6.88.3: Then from the bow there issued forth on every side tridents, maces and clubs, blazing and hard as the thunderbolt.
t.6.88.4: Snares, hammers and maces, and blazing thunderbolts as well, sharp and of many kinds, flew forth like the winds at the end of an age.
t.6.88.5: The glorious and greatly radiant Rāghava, foremost among those who know the supreme weapons, struck down that weapon with the supreme Gāndharva weapon.
t.6.88.6: But when that weapon had been repelled by the great-souled Rāghava, Rāvaṇa, his eyes copper-red with rage, discharged the solar weapon.
t.6.88.7: Then from the bow of the wise Daśagrīva, of terrible speed, there flew forth discuses, shining and huge.
t.6.88.8: By those blazing missiles flying here and there and falling, the sky and the quarters were lit up, as if by the moon, the sun and the planets.
t.6.88.9: But that Rāghava, with floods of arrows, cut down those discuses and the many-hued weapons of Rāvaṇa at the front of the army.
t.6.88.10: But seeing that missile destroyed, Rāvaṇa, the lord of the Rākṣasas, pierced Rāma with ten arrows in all his vital parts.
t.6.88.11: Though pierced by Rāvaṇa with ten arrows loosed from his mighty bow, the greatly glorious Rāghava did not tremble.
t.6.88.12: Then Rāghava, victorious in battle and greatly enraged, pierced Rāvaṇa in all his limbs with many arrows.
t.6.88.13: Meanwhile the mighty Lakṣmaṇa, younger brother of Rāghava and slayer of enemy heroes, grew enraged and took up seven arrows.
t.6.88.14: With those arrows of great speed, the one of great splendor cut the banner of Rāvaṇa, marked with a human head, into many pieces.
t.6.88.15: With an arrow, the glorious and mighty Lakṣmaṇa also struck off the head of the rākṣasa's charioteer, its earrings blazing.
t.6.88.16: And with arrows, with five sharpened shafts, Lakṣmaṇa cut through the bow of that lord of the Rākṣasas, a bow like an elephant's trunk.
t.6.88.17: And Vibhīṣaṇa, leaping forward, struck down with his mace the excellent horses of Rāvaṇa, which resembled dark-blue clouds and were huge as mountains.
t.6.88.18: Swiftly leaping down from his great chariot, whose horses had been slain, the impetuous Rāvaṇa conceived a fierce wrath against his brother.
t.6.88.19: Then the valorous lord of the rākṣasas, possessed of mighty power, hurled at Vibhīṣaṇa a blazing spear, like a flaming thunderbolt.
t.6.88.20: Even before it reached him, Lakṣmaṇa cut it apart with three arrows. Then a great roar arose from the monkeys there on the battlefield.
t.6.88.21: That spear, garlanded with gold, cut into three pieces, fell blazing and scattering sparks, like a great meteor fallen from the sky.
t.6.88.22: Then he seized a mighty spear, most highly esteemed, unapproachable even by Kāla, blazing with its own radiance.
t.6.88.24: Meanwhile the heroic Lakṣmaṇa swiftly came to that Vibhīṣaṇa, who had fallen into peril of his life.
t.6.88.23: Hurled by the swift and mighty, evil-minded Rāvaṇa, that exceedingly great and terrible weapon blazed forth, its radiance equal to Śakra's thunderbolt.
t.6.88.25: To rescue him, the heroic Lakṣmaṇa drew his bow and covered Rāvaṇa, who stood with the spear in his hand, with showers of arrows.
t.6.88.26: Showered with the flood of arrows loosed by the great-souled one, his valour turned back, he could not bring his mind to strike.
t.6.88.27: Seeing that his brother had been rescued by Lakṣmaṇa, Rāvaṇa, standing face to face with Lakṣmaṇa, spoke these words.
t.6.88.28: O you who boast of your strength, since Vibhīṣaṇa has thus been rescued by you, this spear, sparing the rākṣasa, is now hurled down upon you.
t.6.88.29: This spear, marked with red, hurled from my mace-like arm, will pierce your heart and depart, carrying away your life-breaths.
t.6.88.30: Having spoken thus, that spear, hung with eight bells and sounding a mighty roar, fashioned by Maya through his magic power, unfailing and slayer of foes…
t.6.88.31: Aiming it at Lakṣmaṇa, Rāvaṇa, supremely enraged, hurled the spear that seemed to blaze with its splendor, and he roared aloud.
t.6.88.32: Hurled with terrible force, that spear, roaring like the thunderbolt of Śakra, swiftly fell upon Lakṣmaṇa at the forefront of the battle.
t.6.88.33: As the śakti came hurtling toward him, Rāghava addressed it: "May it go well with Lakṣmaṇa! Be fruitless, your force broken!"
t.6.88.34: With tremendous force it fell upon the broad chest of Lakṣmaṇa, blazing and of great radiance, like the tongue of the king of serpents.
t.6.88.35: Then, his heart pierced by the spear, which had sunk in very deep through the force of Rāvaṇa's throw, Lakṣmaṇa fell to the ground.
t.6.88.36: Seeing Lakṣmaṇa in that condition, the greatly radiant Rāghava, standing nearby, became heavy-hearted out of affection for his brother.
t.6.88.37: Having brooded for a moment, his eyes clouded with tears, he became even more enraged, like fire at the end of an age.
t.6.88.38: Reflecting, "This is no time for despondency," Rāghava, firmly resolved upon the slaying of Rāvaṇa, waged a most tumultuous battle.
t.6.88.39: Then Rāma saw Lakṣmaṇa in the great battle, pierced by the spear and smeared with blood, like a mountain with a serpent upon it.
t.6.88.40: Even with great effort, those foremost of monkeys could not crush that spear hurled by the mighty Rāvaṇa, for they were sorely afflicted by the floods of arrows of the swift-handed rākṣasa.
t.6.88.41: Having pierced through Saumitri, the spear entered the surface of the earth. Grasping that terrifying spear with both hands, Rāma, enraged in battle, broke it and forcefully pulled it out.
t.6.88.43: Paying no heed to those arrows, Rāghava embraced Lakṣmaṇa and spoke to Hanumān and Sugrīva: "O best of monkeys, stay here, surrounding Lakṣmaṇa."
t.6.88.42: While he was pulling out the spear, the mighty Rāvaṇa let fly arrows that pierce the vital parts, striking him on all his limbs.
t.6.88.45: In this very moment, before long, I truly promise you, O monkeys: you shall see the world either without Rāvaṇa or without Rāma.
t.6.88.44: This time for valour, long desired by me, has come, like the sight of clouds at the end of the hot season for the longing stokaka bird. Let this evil-souled Daśagrīva, whose resolve is wicked, be slain!
t.6.88.46: The loss of the kingdom, the dwelling in the forest, the wandering about in Daṇḍaka, the violation of Vaidehī, and the encounter with the rākṣasas.
t.6.88.47: The great and dreadful sorrow I have suffered, and the torment like that of hell, all of it I shall cast off today, having slain that Rāvaṇa in battle.
t.6.88.48: For whose sake this army of monkeys was assembled by me, and for whose sake, having slain Vālin in battle, Sugrīva was installed in the kingship.
t.6.88.49: He for whose sake the ocean was crossed and a bridge was built across the sea, that very sinner has today come within the range of my sight on the battlefield.
t.6.88.50: Having come within the range of my eyes, this Rāvaṇa does not deserve to live, just as one who has come within the gaze of a serpent whose very glance is poison cannot survive.
t.6.88.51: O bulls among the vānaras, you who are hard to assail, sit at ease upon the mountain peaks and watch this battle between me and Rāvaṇa.
t.6.88.53: Today I shall perform a deed which the worlds, with all their moving and unmoving beings and with the gods, will tell of for as long as the earth shall endure.
t.6.88.52: Today, in my battle, let the three worlds, together with the Gandharvas, the gods, the sages and the Cāraṇas, behold the true Rāma-hood of Rāma.
t.6.88.54: Having spoken thus, Rāma, composed and resolute, struck the ten-necked Daśagrīva in battle with sharp arrows adorned with refined gold.
t.6.88.55: Then Rāvaṇa showered Rāma with blazing iron arrows and with clubs as well, as a rain-cloud pours down torrents of water.
t.6.88.56: From the arrows released by Rāma and Rāvaṇa, the arrows of the one and the arrows of the other striking against each other, there arose a tumultuous sound.
t.6.88.57: Those arrows of Rāma and Rāvaṇa, shattered and scattered, their tips blazing, fell from the sky onto the surface of the earth.
t.6.88.58: The mighty twanging of the bowstrings striking the palms of those two, Rāma and Rāvaṇa, struck terror into all beings and was like a marvel.
t.6.88.59: Showered with torrents of arrow-nets by the great-souled one wielding the blazing bow, and sorely afflicted, Rāvaṇa, having met him in combat, fled in fear, like a cloud struck by the wind.
